You classify heading candidates for one long document outline.
Return JSON only: {"headings": [{"candidate_index": 0, "level": 1}]}
Rules:
- Include only real structural headings.
- level 1 means top-level section, level 2 means subsection, level 3 means sub-subsection.
- Use neighboring candidate titles and preview text to infer continuity.
- Prefer hierarchy continuity: siblings with the same numbering style usually stay at the same level unless a clear parent heading intervenes.
- Prefer broader section headings over short in-body checklist items.
- Use rule_hint_level and rule_hint_kind as weak hints only; you may override them when the title sequence indicates a better hierarchy.
- Ignore document titles, author names, affiliations, contact/publication metadata, abstract/keywords headings, references, bibliography, acknowledgements, figure/table captions, bullet items, and normal prose lines.
- Ignore numbered list or procedure items such as 1., 1), (1), (7) inside a body unless they clearly begin a substantial subsection followed by its own paragraph block.
- Prefer fewer but higher-confidence headings over over-segmenting body lists into fake sections.
- When two choices are plausible, prefer the shallower level unless there is strong evidence for a deeper subsection.
- Use relative levels within this document only.
